svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.15.4.4 Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Bottom
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.15.4.4 Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Bottom
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.15 FOOTINGS AND FOUNDATIONS
Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Bottom

g.text: Supported at the top by the

svg.text: Flat ICF foundation walls are laterally
supported at the bottom where the wall
(a) supports backfill not more than 1.2 m
(3′-11¼″) in height, (b) is supported at the
footing by a shear key and at the top by the
ground floor framing, or (c) is doweled to the
footing with not less than (i) 15M bars spaced
not more than 1.2 m (3′-11¼″) o.c., or (ii) 10M
bars spaced not more than 600 mm (23⅝″) o.c.
Drawn: flat ICF walls cut through. C and D show the footing before the wall is placed. Sizes other than the limits are illustration only.
